questions.prompt: How many layers does the OSI reference model have?
questions.explanation: The OSI model has 7 layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application. The TCP/IP model has 4.

questions.prompt: Match each protocol to the layer it belongs to.
questions.explanation: IP is layer 3, TCP is layer 4, HTTP is an application-layer protocol, and Ethernet operates at the link layer.

questions.prompt: Order the TCP/IP layers from the topmost (closest to the app) down to the wire.
questions.explanation: The TCP/IP stack, top to bottom, is Application, Transport, Internet, Link.

questions.prompt: Wrapping data with a header at each layer as it moves down the sending stack is called ____.
questions.explanation: Encapsulation adds each layer's header (and the link layer's trailer) on the way down; de-encapsulation strips them on the way up.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the two models are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: The internet is actually built on the TCP/IP model
OSI is mainly a reference and teaching model
TCP is on the same layer as IP
The Transport-layer PDU is called a segment (TCP) or datagram (UDP)

questions.explanation: The internet runs TCP/IP; OSI is a reference model; the transport PDU is a segment/datagram. TCP (transport, 4) and IP (internet, 3) are on different layers.

questions.prompt: What is the Internet-layer (IP) PDU called?
questions.explanation: The IP (Internet-layer) PDU is a packet. A frame is the link-layer PDU, a segment is the transport-layer PDU, and bits are on the physical medium.
